methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates evidence across patient-derived organoids (four CRPC-WNT models), cell lines, CRISPRi knockdown, siRNA with a rescue construct, in vivo xenograft, and orthogonal omics (scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, TCF7L2 ChIP-seq, PRO-cap) with A858 epimer and VHL ligand competition as rigorous negative controls, which supports on-target mechanism. Weaknesses include a single xenograft experiment with small group sizes (n=7 vehicle, n=8 A947), only one animal receiving a single A947 dose with one excluded post-hoc for bacterial infection, reliance on a single patient (DTB-135-PRO) for Hi-C enhancer analysis, and only n=1 or n=2 biological replicates for several key immunoblots. Statistical reporting is adequate (unpaired t-tests, two-way ANOVA, Wilcoxon with Bonferroni correction for scRNA-seq) but lacks effect sizes, confidence intervals, power calculations, multiplicity correction across the many exploratory pairwise comparisons, and pre-specified analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is preclinical/mechanistic research using cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and murine xenografts, which maps to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is nevertheless direct: CRPC-WNT is estimated at 11.7% of CRPC cases in the authors' re-analysis and has no standard of care, and the authors explicitly nominate a CRPC-WNT biomarker-guided strategy and link their findings to an existing phase II trametinib trial (NCT02881242). The translational path is plausible and near-term actionable but has not yet been demonstrated in patients, and SMARCA2/4 PROTAC toxicity and the kidney findings in two treated mice warrant caution.

reporting_quality.justification: For the in vivo component the manuscript reports ethics approval (license BE35/2024), housing, randomization is implied but not explicitly described, blinded histopathology by a board-certified pathologist, exclusion of one animal with a reason given, and humane endpoints (1,000 mm3)—partial ARRIVE adherence but missing explicit randomization method, sample size justification, and full outcome blinding statements. Methods sections for each omics assay are generally detailed with software versions and RRIDs, aiding reproducibility. However, no explicit Data Availability Statement, no GEO/SRA/ArrayExpress accession numbers for the scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, or PRO-cap datasets, and no code repository are visible in the provided text, which is a major reproducibility gap.

novelty_literature.justification: The work extends the Xiao et al. 2022 Nature finding on SWI/SNF PROTACs in CRPC-AR to the recently-defined CRPC-WNT subtype (Tang et al. 2022), and provides a novel mechanistic model in which SMARCA4 loss closes an intragenic TCF7L2 auto-regulatory enhancer and thereby collapses a TCF7L2-directed MAPK/MEK proliferative program—linking chromatin remodeling to a non-canonical TCF7L2 function in prostate cancer. The combined identification of CRPC-WNT dependence on SMARCA4 (not SMARCA2), the TCF7L2 intragenic enhancer, and the MPAS/MEKi connection represents a meaningful combination rather than a first-in-class paradigm shift. It is a solid, gap-filling extension of prior work rather than truly field-defining.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical progression from phenotypic screening to mechanism to in vivo validation, and figure legends describe sample sizes, statistical tests, and scale bars. The text is generally clear, though it is dense with abbreviations (CRPC-AR, CRPC-WNT, CRPC-SCL, CRPC-NE, DNPC, MPAS, PROTAC) and occasional awkward phrasing (e.g., 'Animal was restrained in injection cone'). Figures are appropriately cross-referenced and supplementary material is extensively used.

key_strengths: Multi-modal mechanistic triangulation across scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, TCF7L2 ChIP-seq, PRO-cap, and Hi-C converging on a coherent SMARCA4 to TCF7L2 enhancer to MAPK axis

Use of four independent CRPC-WNT patient-derived organoids with orthogonal perturbations (A947 PROTAC, epimer A858 control, VHL-ligand competition, siRNA with rescue plasmid, CRISPRi) strongly supports on-target effects

Clinically-grounded quantification of CRPC-WNT prevalence (11.7% of CRPC) using integrated scRNA-seq from six independent studies, with explicit link to a biomarker strategy and an existing phase II MEKi trial
key_concerns: No explicit Data Availability Statement or accession numbers visible for the scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, or PRO-cap datasets, and no code repository—major reproducibility gap
Single xenograft experiment with small group sizes (n=7 vs 8), a single A947 dose, one animal excluded post-hoc, and kidney fibrosis in two treated mice that is ambiguously attributed
Enhancer analysis in primary tumors relies on a single WNT-classified biopsy (DTB-135-PRO) of three, limiting generalizability
Statistics lack effect sizes, confidence intervals, power calculations, and multiplicity correction across many exploratory comparisons; several key immunoblots are n=1 or n=2
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, mechanistically coherent preclinical study with clear translational implications but not practice-changing; fits tier 2 (Cancer Research, Clinical Cancer Research, Nat Commun) with minor revisions principally to add an explicit data/code availability statement, strengthen statistics, and temper the single-patient Hi-C inference.
